deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Hilbert has just raised the 'important question' of approximating two functions phi(x), psi(x) simultaneously by rational functions with a common denominator. He reduces it to finding polynomials P, Q, R such that the remainder A := P*phi + Q*psi + R vanishes to as high an order N as possible, at x = infinity. In modern terms this is the type-I Hermite-Pade problem. If phi is a distinguished solution of a 2nd-order linear ODE and psi = phi', he proposes deriving a 3rd-order linear ODE for P. He uses 'the method of p. 43': a certain 3rd-order linear differential expression must be divisible by P.

(1) This page opens by finishing that sentence. The 3rd-order ODE found in this way should also be satisfied by the remainder A. This is stated without proof.

(2) Irrationality programme. Fix a rational x and form the sequence of approximations of degree n:
- (E_n) P_n*phi + Q_n*psi + R_n = A_n
- (E_{n+1}) P_{n+1}*phi + Q_{n+1}*psi + R_{n+1} = A_{n+1}
Hilbert writes A_{n-1} on the right of the second line; this is an index slip.
Eliminating psi [explicit step mine] means taking Q_{n+1}*E_n - Q_n*E_{n+1}:
(P_n Q_{n+1} - P_{n+1} Q_n)*phi + (R_n Q_{n+1} - R_{n+1} Q_n) = Q_{n+1} A_n - Q_n A_{n+1}.
Hilbert's 'Grösse' Q_n A_{n-1} - Q_{n+1} A_n is this right-hand side up to sign, in his indexing.
The resulting linear form in 1 and phi has rational coefficients at rational x. If, after clearing denominators, it stays nonzero and tends to 0, then phi(x) is irrational. Hilbert only says that A_n, and the combination above, must become 'sufficiently small'.

(3) Markov-type functions. Take phi = int_{-1}^{1} u(xi)/(x-xi) dxi and psi = int_{-1}^{1} v(xi)/(x-xi) dxi. Then [derivation mine, certainly intended]:
- P(x) phi(x) = int P(xi)u(xi)/(x-xi) dxi + (polynomial in x), and similarly for Q psi.
- Choosing R = -(the polynomial parts) gives A(x) = int_{-1}^{1} (P(xi)u(xi) + Q(xi)v(xi))/(x-xi) dxi = sum_{k>=0} x^{-k-1} int xi^k (P u + Q v) dxi.
- Hence A = O(x^{-N-1}) iff int_{-1}^{1} xi^k (P(xi)u(xi) + Q(xi)v(xi)) dxi = 0 for k = 0..N-1.
This is the 'entsprechende Orthogonalitätseigenschaft von P_n': type-I multiple orthogonality of the pair (P_n, Q_n) with respect to the two weights u, v.

(4) Pairs of functions. Hilbert proposes regarding [-1,1] twice, as two independent intervals. Functions on this doubled interval are pairs (f, g), and the inner product is int f1 f2 u + int g1 g2 v. Read so, the list (1,1); (1,x); (x,1); (1,x^2); ... is the staircase ordering of the polynomial pairs (P, Q) used in the orthogonalization.
He conjectures the analogue of the Sturm-Liouville expansion theorem: any pair of functions can be expanded simultaneously in the pairs of eigenfunctions, with one common set of Fourier coefficients. He remarks this probably yields the simplest examples of 'simultaneous orthogonal or polar systems'. 'Polar' is his term from the theory of polar integral equations.
errors: Index slip: the second relation should read P_{n+1} phi + Q_{n+1} psi + R_{n+1} = A_{n+1}, not A_{n-1}. With that correction the eliminated quantity is Q_{n+1}A_n - Q_n A_{n+1}, matching Hilbert's expression up to sign.

Unjustified/unstated: the irrationality argument also needs the eliminated linear form (P_nQ_{n+1} - P_{n+1}Q_n)phi + (...) to be nonzero, i.e. a nonvanishing determinant / independence of consecutive approximants. It also needs control of the denominators of the coefficients at rational x. Smallness alone does not suffice.
Unproved claim: that the remainder A satisfies the same 3rd-order ODE as P is asserted without argument. It holds in classical cases such as Pade/Legendre-type situations but is not automatic.

'A klein' is ambiguous: the construction makes A small at x = infinity (high order of vanishing), whereas the irrationality argument needs smallness at a fixed rational x as n grows. That needs separate estimates, which Hilbert acknowledges only as 'wäre nötig'.
The expansion theorem for pairs is a conjecture ('gelangt ... zu einem Satze'), not proved here.

results.what: Simultaneous rational approximation of two functions with common denominator via P phi + Q psi + R = A of maximal order
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite (1873, transcendence of e), Pade (1892-94), systematic theory by Mahler (1930s), Jager, Coates

results.what: Irrationality proof for phi at rational x by eliminating psi from consecutive simultaneous approximations and requiring small remainders
results.modern_name: Diophantine/irrationality method via Hermite-Pade approximants (Siegel-type method; nonvanishing-determinant argument)
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite, Siegel 1929 (Bessel J0, J0' — exactly a solution of a 2nd-order ODE together with its derivative), later Apery, Beukers, Rivoal

results.what: 3rd-order linear ODE for the denominator polynomial P (and remainder A) when phi solves a 2nd-order ODE and psi = phi'
results.modern_name: Differential equations for Hermite-Pade polynomials / multiple orthogonal polynomials
results.usually_credited_to: Classical cases: Pade/Laguerre; general theory 20th c. (e.g. Coates, Chudnovsky, Van Assche et al.)

results.what: For Cauchy transforms phi, psi of weights u, v on [-1,1], the approximation condition equals int xi^k (P u + Q v) dxi = 0
results.modern_name: Type-I multiple orthogonal polynomials (Nikishin/Angelesco-type systems on one interval)
results.usually_credited_to: Mahler (perfect systems, 1930s, publ. 1968), Nikishin, Aptekarev, de Bruin, Van Assche (1980s-2000s)

results.what: Treating the interval twice, functions as pairs, and conjecturing simultaneous expansion of an arbitrary pair in eigenfunction pairs with common Fourier coefficients
results.modern_name: Eigenfunction expansion for vector-valued (system) Sturm-Liouville/integral operators; vector orthogonality
results.usually_credited_to: Vector Sturm-Liouville theory (20th c.); Hilbert's own polar integral equations (1906)

deep.surprise_reason: Hermite-Pade approximation and its use for irrationality go back to Hermite. Hilbert's own transcendence work makes interest in it natural. But this page sketches several things not attributed to him: the type-I multiple-orthogonality characterization for Cauchy transforms, a planned irrationality argument via elimination between consecutive approximants for phi together with phi' of a 2nd-order ODE (strongly reminiscent of Siegel 1929), and a vector expansion theorem. These anticipate later developments (Siegel; Mahler; multiple orthogonal polynomials). However, it is only a programmatic sketch with no estimates, nonvanishing argument or concrete theorem, and the notebook's date is uncertain, so the score stays moderate.

1/(x-xi) = sum_k xi^k x^{-k-1}, so A = sum_k x^{-k-1} int xi^k (P u + Q v) dxi and A = O(x^{-N-1}) iff the first N moments vanish
